children: Continued fiscal concerns could weigh on demand at Japan's sale of 20-year government bonds Tuesday, says Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities strategist Yasuhiro Nakatani. "Caution over potential increases in government bond issuance is likely to linger, given scope for the final fiscal 2027 budget expenditure to swell and ongoing uncertainty surrounding funding sources for consumption tax cuts," he says. "On the other hand, the pause in global sovereign yield increases is expected to underpin investor demand." The Finance Ministry is slated to auction 700 billion yen of 20-year bonds Tuesday. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
